title: Compact-support base change over a finite extension
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $I=(\varpi)$, using the adic datum of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Let
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X'&\xrightarrow{g'}&X\\
f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
Y'&\xrightarrow{g}&Y
\end{array}
$$
be a compact-support base-change square [def-cbc-compact-support-square], with $f$ separated of finite type. Require that all four schemes are noetherian and finite-dimensional and that $\ell$ is invertible on them. No smoothness, properness or finite-type hypothesis on $g$ is imposed.

Write $\mathcal C_T=\Dbc(T_{\Proet},A)$ for the completed integral category of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], and use its raw rationalization $\Dbc(T,E)=\mathcal C_T[1/\varpi]$ [def-weil-pbc-rational-category]. The integral operations are completed pullback [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] and compact-support direct image $Rf_!=Rp_*j_!$ for a compactification of $f$ [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification], and their base-changed versions. On the rational categories use their $E$-linear extensions [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport]. Define the rational compact-support exchange to be the extension of the specified completed integral exchange [def-cbc-completed-exchange-map]. Then for every $K\in\Dbc(X,E)$ its component is an isomorphism
$$
\Ex_{!,E}(K):Lg^*Rf_!K\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_!Lg'^*K
\quad\text{in }\Dbc(Y',E).
$$
It is natural in every rational morphism. For integral representatives $M,N$ equipped with a rational isomorphism identifying them, the two components agree under the isomorphisms induced by the two composite functors; this is independence of the integral lattice. Identity and pasted-square coherence hold for squares whose schemes lie in the stated category domains.

proof.text: Identify the completed coefficient isomorphism with the datum isomorphism by its quotient projections. Uniqueness of left adjoints identifies the open-extension functors. Apply the integral compact-support uniform-restriction theorem and its strictly-full landing predicate to obtain compact-support preservation.

proof.text: For a horizontal map U to V use the proper identity square with fibre dimension zero. The valuation-ring quotient has characteristic l by the DVR theorem, and stalkwise invertibility gives global invertibility. The third conclusion of actual-coefficient constructible preservation gives completed-pullback preservation; this theorem needs no separate common-interval hypothesis.

proof.text: Prove scalar compatibility on ordinary reduction towers by the tensor generators and the reduction unit. Scalar endomorphisms descend to the universal left-derived functor by right-Kan-extension uniqueness. Tower pullback and inverse limit are linear by their adjunctions. Open extension and derived direct image are linear by their linear right and left adjoints. Additivity descends to the derived categories; restrict these properties through the full inclusions.

proof.text: Use intrinsic completeness of each bounded constructible object to obtain its complete-property witness for every generating tuple. The unit-normalization equation for the completed open exchange is tuple-free. Restrict the exchange for a second tuple to the first full complete subcategory and use uniqueness to identify the components. The datum transport and ordered proper/open composite preserve this equality.

proof.text: Choose a generating tuple for the finitely generated ideal. Apply complete compact-support base change to each bounded constructible object and its retained etale origins. The two endpoints land in the full bounded constructible category by the first two steps, so its inverse belongs to this category. Integral naturality assembles these components into a natural isomorphism.

source.place: Proof, sole paragraph; integral constructible landing and scalar-localization argument made explicit

proof.text: Transport the integral natural transformation through scalar localization. Each localized component is the image of an integral isomorphism and is therefore invertible. Generator independence gives the specified component formula for every tuple. Naturality is naturality of this transported transformation for every rational morphism, and hence gives lattice independence.

proof.text: Apply the localization map on the full integral Hom module to the integral identity, horizontal-pasting, and vertical-pasting equalities. Establish the required endpoint membership by the preservation results above. Congruence gives exactly the three rational coherence formulas.
